title: A depolarizing choir sings in Gaussian harmony
authors: Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Sujeet Bhalerao, Sungjai Lee, Felix Leditzky, Debbie Leung, Luke Schaeffer, Graeme Smith
abstract: We study the noise threshold for positive quantum capacity for the qubit depolarizing channel. We explore analytically the action of the qubit depolarizing channel on the symmetric subspaces of the input qubits, in the limit of asymptotically many uses of the channel. We observe the emergence of a bosonic Gaussian channel. Furthermore, the codes previously developed for the depolarizing channel can be translated to codes for the emergent Gaussian channel, and it is easier to further optimize these codes for the simpler emergent Gaussian channel. Translating these codes back to the depolarizing channel leads to extremely good input states for the coherent information of the depolarizing channel producing new lower bounds on the noise threshold for positive capacity. In addition to improved lower bounds on the threshold, this newly found link between depolarizing noise and Gaussian channels offers a novel perspective contributing to our understanding of these symmetric codes.
summary: This paper analyzes the noise threshold for the quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel by demonstrating its asymptotic equivalence to a Gaussian channel. By leveraging this connection, the authors derive a significantly improved lower bound for the noise threshold. This work offers a new theoretical perspective on symmetric quantum codes under noise.
main_problem: The primary goal is to determine the noise threshold ($p_{th}$) for achieving positive quantum capacity for the qubit depolarizing channel.
main_result: The authors derive a new, improved lower bound on the noise threshold, establishing $p_{th} \gtrsim 0.2029$, by linking the depolarizing channel to an emergent Gaussian channel.
method: The analysis uses representation theory (Schur-Weyl duality) to show that the depolarizing channel action asymptotically approximates a Gaussian thermal attenuator channel, allowing the use of Gaussian channel bounds.
model_or_system: The system under study is the qubit depolarizing channel, $D_p$, acting on symmetric subspaces of multiple qubits. The analysis relates this discrete channel to continuous bosonic Gaussian channels.
key_observables: Quantum capacity ($Q$), Coherent Information ($I_c$), and the noise threshold ($p_{th}$).
important_parameters: Noise parameter $p$ (or transmissivity $\eta$), and the number of channel uses $M 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the asymptotic equivalence between the depolarizing channel and the Gaussian channel, and the use of concentration inequalities for bounding errors.
figures_summary: Figure 1 (mentioned) illustrates the historical improvement of the lower bound for the threshold over time.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the action of the depolarizing channel on symmetric subspaces, showing its equivalence to a Gaussian channel, and then using the coherent information of the Gaussian channel to establish a rigorous lower bound on the quantum capacity threshold.
why_interesting: The novel link established between discrete depolarizing noise and continuous Gaussian channels provides a powerful new mathematical tool for analyzing quantum error correction thresholds in open quantum systems.
